quotes.quote: For fiscal year 2027, we anticipate increased capital investments as we transition to newer nodes to meet the demand and technology needs of our product portfolio.

capex_to_revenue.why: Capex was only 0.9% of revenue in FY2026 and 1.9% pooled, but management says it will invest more as it moves to newer nodes. I use 2.5%, with the wafer-making equipment sitting mostly in the ventures.

quotes.quote: we believe they reduce certain elements of industry cyclicality

fade_years.why: The margin mean-reverts over a long period, not at once. NBM contracts and multi-year volume commitments should slow the reversion, so I use a ten-year fade.

quotes.quote: declining average selling prices, volatile demand, technological change

long_run_op_margin.why: Past margins were -33%, -7% and -19% before the 61% base year, so the 5-year median is about -13%. Applying the cyclical base rate (keeping about half of the gap above the median) gives roughly 24%. This is helped by the NBM contracts, the AI demand structure and the Kioxia cost-plus wafer supply, and limited by commodity competition.

quotes.quote: GAAP operating margin(1) | 79.6% | 78.5% | 7.6%

op_margin.why: The latest quarter's operating margin is 79.6% and Q2 guidance implies a similar gross margin, so year 1 stays high at 0.77. After that I fade it as pricing normalises and operating costs rise, since variable pay follows profits and the company is adding R&D.

quotes.quote: Return on new investment at which growth adds no value
We hold a 49.9% ownership position in each of the Flash Ventures entities.

return_on_new_investment_long_run.why: The base-year return on tangible capital of 1.0 is a peak-price artifact. In the long run, new capital goes mainly into Flash Ventures notes and node transitions with the Kioxia partner, which should earn above the 11% hurdle but far below the current level.

quotes.quote: Expect second quarter 2027 revenue to be in the range of $12.2 billion to $12.6 billion
Total products sold increased by mid-teens percent on an exabyte basis.

rev_growth.why: Year 1 is largely locked in by run-rate: Q1 revenue was $11.0B and Q2 guidance is $12.2-12.6B, so FY2027 is roughly $45-50B, about 130% above the $20.2B base. Growth in FY2026 came from pricing, with volume up only mid-teens, so I assume prices ease in year 2 and fall more in year 3 as NAND supply catches up, then a modest recovery.

quotes.quote: long-run nominal growth anchor g_anchor 0.0375

terminal_growth.why: A mature NAND memory business should grow near long-run nominal growth. Data storage demand growth supports this, while price deflation per bit holds it back.

risks.risk: NAND price collapse or an AI data-center spending pause drives revenue and margins back to the historical industry norm sooner than assumed
Pricing-led revenue reverses sharply in year 3 and volume does not offset it; NBM customers fail to honour purchase commitments
Supply-side competition (Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron, YMTC, Kioxia) adds capacity and growth flattens in the long run

debt_level_representative.why: The term loan was repaid, the $1.5B revolver is undrawn ("As of October 2, 2026, there were no amounts outstanding under the Revolving Credit Facility."), and the company holds net cash and is generating very large operating cash flow.

situation.margin_position: The margin is at a cyclical peak. Revenue rose far faster than shipped volume (exabytes), so price and mix, not unit cost, produced the profit. Cost of revenue was almost flat while the gross margin went from 29.8% to 85.0%. The company's own five-year margin history is negative, so the current level is far above the through-cycle norm.

tax_rate_representative.why: The 12% FY2026 rate benefits from Malaysian tax holidays that expire 2028-2031 and the company expects to be subject to the corporate alternative minimum tax in FY2027; guidance already points to 14.3% (quote: "Tax Expense (2) | N/A | 14.3%").

situation.why: FY2026 revenue was $20.2B at a 61% operating margin, after a 175% revenue jump driven mostly by NAND pricing, and the latest quarter is already far above that year. Earlier fiscal years had negative margins, and the base year includes an $808M mark-to-market equity gain. Long-term NBM contracts may soften the cycle but, by management's own statement, do not remove demand and pricing risk, so I expect a sizeable fade after year 2.

Pooled over those years: capital expenditure / revenue 0.0190

capex_to_revenue.why: Direct capex has been tiny (0.9% of revenue), but management expects more investment for node transitions, and Flash Ventures funding adds to cash needs. Pooled history is 1.9%, so I use 2.5%.

quotes.quote: we believe they reduce certain elements of industry cyclicality

fade_years.why: Ten years lets the margin and growth converge slowly from the peak toward cycle-average levels. Long-term agreements may extend the normalization.

quotes.quote: We compete with vertically-integrated suppliers such as Kioxia, Micron Technology, Inc., Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd., SK Hynix, Inc., Yangtze Memory Technologies Co., Ltd. and numerous smaller companies that assemble flash into products.

long_run_op_margin.why: The company's own earlier margins were negative and it competes with Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron, Kioxia and YMTC. The base rate says a cyclical margin above its median keeps about half of the gap. Long-term agreements and AI demand justify a margin well above the historical median, so I set 27% with a wide range.

quotes.quote: Gross profit margin increased 4,100 basis points in 2026 compared to 2025 primarily due to higher sales and higher pricing.

op_margin.why: The margin starts near the current 80% because Q2 guidance is for gross margin of 84.4%-85.4% on operating expenses of $677-745 million. It fades as pricing normalizes, because costs are largely fixed or cost-plus while selling prices drive profit. The multi-year long-term agreements slow the decline but do not remove cyclicality.

quotes.quote: Return on new investment at which growth adds no value
We hold a 49.9% ownership position in each of the Flash Ventures entities.

return_on_new_investment_long_run.why: The company is asset-light because wafer equipment sits in Flash Ventures, so the current return on tangible capital is very high. Competition and node-transition spending should pull the return on new investment toward a level above the 11% break-even but far below the current return.

quotes.quote: Expect second quarter 2027 revenue to be in the range of $12.2 billion to $12.6 billion
Total products sold increased by almost 10% on an exabyte basis.

rev_growth.why: Q1 FY2027 revenue was $11.0 billion and Q2 is guided to $12.2-12.6 billion, so FY2027 is already running at about $46-48 billion, roughly +130% on FY2026. After that I assume NAND prices mean-revert: revenue falls in years 2 and 3, then recovers, because the growth has been price-led, not volume-led.

quotes.quote: long-run nominal growth anchor g_anchor 0.0375

terminal_growth.why: A mature memory supplier should grow roughly with nominal GDP and data storage growth, near the long-run anchor, with some haircut for NAND price deflation per bit.

risks.risk: NAND prices fall sharply as supply catches up or AI data-center buying pauses, collapsing revenue and margin; fixed Flash Ventures costs make the downside worse
Price-led revenue reverses faster than assumed, with a deeper contraction in year 3
Higher capex and Flash Ventures funding for node transitions, plus competitors' supply additions, push capital intensity up

debt_level_representative.why: The term loan was repaid and the $1.5 billion revolver is undrawn, so zero debt looks sustainable given cash generation, though the Flash Ventures guarantees are an off-balance-sheet obligation.

situation.margin_position: The FY2026 operating margin of 61% is far above the company's own history of -33% to -7% from FY2023 to FY2025. Cost of revenue was almost flat while revenue per gigabyte jumped, so NAND price and mix, not cost, drive the margin. That is a cyclical peak that long-term agreements may only partly hold.

tax_rate_representative.why: The 12% FY2026 rate benefits from Malaysian tax holidays that expire 2028-2031, and the company expects to pay the corporate alternative minimum tax in fiscal 2027.

situation.why: FY2026 revenue rose 175% while volume rose only mid-teens percent, and the Q1 FY2027 gross margin of 85% rests on pricing, so the base year is a price-driven peak. Prior years were loss-making. A cyclical margin above its long-run level should keep only part of that gap, so the base-year margin is not a steady state.

Net cash used in financing was (5,755), so cash still rose by 374. A 14 billion repurchase program was approved and is expected to be funded by operating cash flows.
quotes: Our share repurchase program may not enhance shareholder value and could affect the price of our common stock and reduce our financial flexibility.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the 8-K and 10-Q; the conclusion that no near-term maturities exist is inferred from the absence of other borrowings in the balance sheet.
financial_health.claim: No debt appears to fall due soon, and the funding backstop has been extended. The 1,500.0 million revolver is undrawn, and its maturity was extended to September 9, 2031. It has no amortization, carries a maximum leverage ratio covenant and is secured by company and subsidiary assets.
quotes: The Revolving Credit Facility will mature on September 9, 2031, at which time the commitments thereunder shall be terminated, and will not have any amortization.

financial_health.basis: Obligation stated in the 10-K business section; cash amounts stated in the statements; the guarantee risk is stated only as a risk factor heading in the packet.
financial_health.claim: A significant non-debt commitment is the company's obligation to Flash Ventures. The company must pay half of the ventures' fixed costs whatever output it buys. It also funds the ventures through notes receivable, with issuances of 151 in the quarter, and the notes and investments carried on the balance sheet were 827 (table in millions).
quotes: In addition, we are obligated to pay for half of Flash Ventures’ fixed costs regardless of the output we choose to purchase.

growth_thesis.basis: Figures are stated in the cited tables. The persistence of demand is management's expectation, not an outcome.
growth_thesis.claim: AI-driven Datacenter demand is the largest incremental driver. Datacenter revenue was 4,802 in the latest quarter against 269 a year earlier (table in millions), and Datacenter exabytes sold rose almost 330%. For this to continue, AI infrastructure demand must keep requiring NAND storage; management says it expects that demand to persist.
quotes: We expect AI-driven demand to persist through calendar year 2027 and beyond.

growth_thesis.basis: Percentages are stated in the 10-Q MD&A and the release. The condition that pricing must hold is inferred from the pricing-versus-volume split.
growth_thesis.claim: Pricing is a major driver, with total volume contributing far less. Revenue rose 378% while total exabytes sold rose almost 10%, and Datacenter revenue per gigabyte rose almost 320%. For this to continue, pricing and product-mix gains must hold, since the growth is not mainly total volume.
quotes: These shifts have positively impacted our business, and we expect these favorable pricing trends and product mix shifts to have a positive impact on our revenue and cash flows from operations.
Sequential revenue growth came approximately one-third from higher volumes and two-thirds from higher pricing.

growth_thesis.basis: Segment figures are stated in the release and 10-Q. The allocation mechanism is stated in the Operational Update, and its durability is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Mix shift toward higher-value Datacenter and Edge customers drives growth. Datacenter was 4,802 and Edge 5,832 in the quarter, while Consumer fell to 397 from 652 (table in millions). For this to continue, management must keep allocating supply to those end markets, and Consumer decline must not offset the gains.
quotes: Revenue outperformance was driven by both our mix shift toward higher-value customers

growth_thesis.basis: Figures are stated in the income statement. The leverage explanation is inferred from the lines.
growth_thesis.claim: Cost discipline lets revenue growth convert to profit. Gross margin was 85.0% against 29.8% a year earlier. Cost of revenue was 1,653 against 1,621, and operating expenses were 598 against 511 (table in millions), so operating income reached 8,780 against 176. For this to continue, cost of revenue and opex must stay low relative to revenue.

growth_thesis.basis: The terms and the benefit are stated by management. The contract-liability rise is stated in the balance sheet, and linking it to NBMs is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Long-term New Business Model (NBM) agreements underpin growth visibility. They commit customers to stated volumes, mostly over multi-year periods, with financial guarantees. Non-current contract liabilities rose to 752 from 393 (table in millions). For this to continue, customers must honor purchase obligations and the agreements must keep being signed.
quotes: As NBMs are expected to become our predominant way of doing business, we believe that this business model will contribute to greater predictability of revenue, support production planning, and enhance supply assurance for our customers.

growth_thesis.basis: Supply dependence and the capex intent are stated. That volume depends on supply is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Supply capacity is a necessary condition for further volume growth. All flash memory comes from the Kioxia joint ventures, and management anticipates increased capital investment as it transitions to newer nodes. Notes receivable issuances to Flash Ventures were 151 in the quarter (table in millions). For growth to continue, Flash Ventures output and node transitions must keep pace with demand.
quotes: All of our flash-based memory is obtained from our joint ventures with Kioxia, which provide us with leading-edge, high-quality flash memory wafers.
For fiscal year 2027, we anticipate increased capital investments as we transition to newer nodes to meet the demand and technology needs of our product portfolio.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the earnings release. It is guidance, not a result.
growth_thesis.claim: Near-term guidance implies continued sequential growth, but it depends on the drivers above holding. Management expects second quarter revenue of $12.2 billion to $12.6 billion, after first quarter revenue of $11.0 billion.
quotes: Expect second quarter 2027 revenue to be in the range of $12.2 billion to $12.6 billion

material_events.basis: stated in the 8-K earnings release and 8-K Item 8.01; completion is not shown in the packet
material_events.claim: Sandisk announced an eight-for-one forward stock split of its common stock, with post-split trading expected to begin at the market open on the following trading day. The evidence does not show that the split was completed.
quotes: Announced today an eight-for-one forward stock split, effective November 19, 2026, to make stock more accessible, including to employees through its employee stock purchase plan.

material_events.claim: The Board approved a $14 billion share repurchase program, which the company may suspend or discontinue at any time.
quotes: On August 5, 2026, the Company announced that its Board of Directors had approved a $14 billion (exclusive of fees and commissions) share repurchase program (the “Repurchase Program”).

material_events.basis: stated in the earnings release and shown in the cash flow statement
material_events.claim: In the fiscal first quarter, Sandisk repurchased about 3.2 million shares and returned $5.0 billion to stockholders; the cash flow statement shows the repurchase outflow.
quotes: Returned $5.0 billion to stockholders through the repurchase of approximately 3.2 million shares during the quarter.

material_events.basis: stated in the 8-K Item 1.01 and the 10-Q MD&A
material_events.claim: Sandisk entered into Amendment No. 1 to its loan agreement. It refinanced the revolving credit facility in full at an aggregate principal amount of $1,500.0 million and extended maturity to September 9, 2031. No amounts were outstanding as of October 2, 2026.
quotes: Amendment No. 1 provides for a revolving credit facility (the “Revolving Credit Facility”) comprising an aggregate principal amount of $1,500.0 million in revolving commitments, which commitments refinanced in full the revolving commitments outstanding under the Loan Agreement prior to Amendment No. 1.

material_events.claim: Sandisk settled the remaining Term Loan Facility in full using cash on hand and recognized a loss on debt extinguishment of $46 million.
quotes: On March 4, 2026, the Company settled in full the remaining outstanding principal amounts of the Term Loan Facility, plus accrued interest, using cash on hand.

In connection with the early settlement of the Term Loan Facility, the Company recognized a loss on debt extinguishment of $46 million resulting from the write-off of the remaining unamortized issuance costs.

material_events.claim: After the separation from WDC, Sandisk recorded a goodwill impairment charge of $1.8 billion. No goodwill impairment was recorded in fiscal 2026.
quotes: Consequently, we recorded a goodwill impairment charge of $1.8 billion during the fiscal year ended June 27, 2025.

material_events.claim: Sandisk entered into long-term New Business Model agreements with several Datacenter and Edge customers, committing both sides to stated volumes mostly over multi-year periods.
quotes: Commencing in the second half of fiscal year 2026, we entered into long-term agreements, which we also refer to as New Business Models, or “NBMs,” with several Datacenter and Edge customers.

risks.basis: Pricing dependence is stated in P4 and P10; the effect of a reversal is inferred from the income statement structure.
risks.claim: Results depend heavily on NAND pricing: Datacenter revenue per gigabyte rose almost 320% in the latest quarter, and most of the prior quarter's sequential growth came from higher pricing rather than volume.
quotes: Revenue per gigabyte increased by almost 320%.
Sequential revenue growth came approximately one-third from higher volumes and two-thirds from higher pricing.

risks.basis: Stated in P4 and P2; the balance-sheet link is inferred from F1.
risks.claim: The New Business Model long-term agreements, expected to become the predominant way of doing business, carry execution, demand and customer-performance risk and have already absorbed cash through prepayments and deposits.
quotes: While these agreements do not eliminate the risks associated with customer demand, market conditions, or operational execution, we believe they reduce certain elements of industry cyclicality and support our long-term strategic and financial objectives.
Long-term agreements, which we also refer to as New Business Models or “NBMs”, expose us to certain execution, financial, and market risks, which could be significant.

risks.basis: Stated in P1; the downside effect is inferred.

we are obligated to pay for half of Flash Ventures’ fixed costs regardless of the output we choose to purchase
